title: Sanitization, Validation, and Escaping
keywords: choosing controls appropriate to the destination
subtopics: Choosing controls appropriate to the destination.
learning_outcomes: Explain what sanitization, validation, and escaping contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: differences between validation and sanitization.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Form values arrive as untrusted strings and may be absent, malformed, or repeated. Normalize them, validate business rules on the server, preserve safe user input when showing errors, and escape values on output. In this lesson, focus on differences between validation and sanitization; then compare it with contextual output escaping. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use sanitization, validation, and escaping when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating input validation as output escaping.
common_mistakes.why: A value can be valid data and still be unsafe in an HTML or JavaScript output context.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate shape and business rules at input boundaries, then apply context-appropriate output encoding.

common_mistakes.why: A request can be sent without the original form or browser UI.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat all security-relevant validation and authorization on the server.

common_mistakes.problem: Returning internal error details to the browser.
common_mistakes.why: Stack traces and configuration values may expose sensitive information.
common_mistakes.fix: Log safe diagnostics server-side and return a generic, useful response.
